body:
PR #2029 (BUG-1476) APPROVED AND MERGED as 0b474a66d1 at 21:21. It surfaced in my sweep as unheld-and-mergeable — it had been CONFLICTING/DIRTY all evening and someone rebased it. Independence: codex+claude authored, I implemented none of it, no prior verdict existed.

THE FINDING I WOULD LEAD WITH IS ABOUT THE CHECK, NOT THE CODE. A tree-diff makes this PR look catastrophic:

    git diff origin/main d09842ed85
      review_verdict.rs          -238
      review_verdict_tests.rs    -423

That is exactly the STORY-1391 work I merged twelve minutes earlier. It is a TREE difference caused by the branch being 2 commits behind, not a merge outcome — the commit does not touch review_verdict.rs at all, verified by a name-only listing returning zero matches, so the merge keeps main's version.

Anyone reviewing this by tree-diff refuses it for a revert that cannot happen. I nearly wrote that finding before checking which files the commit actually contains. It is the same shape as reading a cumulative patch on #2045 and seeing one line both added and removed: the instrument answers a different question from the one being asked, and its answer is alarming rather than wrong.

THE COMMIT'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS TRUE. It says BUG-1476's production fix already landed under BUG-1445 and this branch is reduced to the missing test. On main: blocking_rework_verdict at lib.rs:32641, called from the phase-1 path at 87305. The rename to rework_guard_verdict was the only difference and was correctly resolved to main.

SIXTEEN OF SEVENTEEN FILES ARE ALREADY-ON-MAIN CONTENT re-applied by a rebase onto a stale base — the prose-classifier script, its test, its doc, and a dozen one-line marker comments, all byte-identical to origin/main, checked file by file. Harmless on merge, but it makes a 37-line test read as a 221-line change.

NON-BLOCKING AND WORTH KNOWING: the new test's justifying comment is false. It claims "the positive case above has no competing spec-keyed verdict". That case is pr_keyed_reviewer_verdict_arms_rework_guard at line 39 of the same file, and it records STORY-1350 Approved with the summary "stale spec-keyed verdict" alongside PR-1974 RequestChanges. Since the spec-keyed verdict is Approved, its kind assertion already discriminates first-found from first-blocking.

I was specific there because I got this exact question wrong earlier tonight — I told both of you #2029's masking test covered a case main lacked, then corrected myself that main already had it. This is the third time I have been to this particular file and the first time I read both tests side by side.

THE TEST IS STILL WORTH HAVING and its value is one assertion rather than a new scenario: assert_eq!(verdict.reviewed_sha, Some("abc123")) pins WHICH verdict came back, where the existing test only pins the kind. Strictly stronger on the same scenario. The comment should say that instead of claiming absent coverage.

Both required contexts green — merge-hold-gate and Build (ubuntu-latest). Build (windows-latest) was pending and is the path-filtered informational matrix, not required; I recorded that in the verdict rather than waiting on it.

THAT CLOSES THE LAST ACTIONABLE ITEM I HAD. Three merges tonight: #2041, #2045, #2029.
subject: #2029 APPROVED and MERGED as 0b474a66d1 - and a tree-diff makes it look like it reverts #2045 when the commit never touches that file
